entries.0eda03be95f65257: This is a business based mainly in Japan that manufactures and sells building materials such as sashes for windows, entrance doors, shutters, gates, carports, and curtain walls, and also provides housing-related services including franchise chain development for local builders, construction contracting, and real estate management. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥518,432 million, a slight decrease from ¥521,002 million in the previous fiscal year. entries.5689bba9c3211e5f: This business manufactures and sells water-related equipment, including sanitary ware, shower toilets, faucet fittings, bathtubs, and unit baths, as well as exterior and interior tiles for housing and buildings. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥808,842 million, the largest of the three reportable segments, and a slight increase from ¥802,586 million in the previous fiscal year. In Japan, sales to renovation markets for sanitary ware and bathroom products were firm, and revenue increased. Overseas, in Europe, sales improved in most product categories, including faucet fittings, and unit sales increased; demand also continued in the Middle East and India. In the United States, revenue fell due to the previous year's transfer of the bathtub business and a delayed recovery in the renovation market, and in China, a slump in the property market compounded these factors, so overseas as a whole was roughly flat. European subsidiaries, including Grohe AG in Germany, are also included in this business.

entries.57b7f2ea9b4f13e9: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,510,704 million, up 0.4% from ¥1,504,697 million in the previous year. In Japan, sales of new housing construction were sluggish, but renovation demand, mainly for water-related products, was solid. Overseas, revenue improved in Europe, the Middle East and India, while the United States saw a decline due to the transfer of the bathtub business in the previous year, and China was hit by the sluggish real estate market.
